newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Differential expected to widen.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Differential expected to widen.

text.p: Prices at the top end of the barrel were steady on Tuesday but traders expected the light distillates spread to widen amid healthy gasoline demand and ample naphtha supplies.
Traders said gasoline prices were around $2.00 per barrel higher than naphtha barrels, but the spread may widen out to as much as $2.50.
Regional gasoline demand was supporting Singapore gasoline prices with few availabilities remaining in February, traders said.
An aggressive offer at $25.20 per barrel for 50,000 barrels of 95-octane lifting late February, 15 cents lower than Monday's bid, was quickly traded, sources said.

Sources said India was expected to announce a tender to buy four cargoes - one to the east coast and three to the west coast - of 25,000 tonnes each of 87-octane leaded gasoline for March delivery because of the turnaround of a cracker at Bombay. India had tendered to buy three cargoes for February.
Refinery turnarounds in the Philippines have also absorbed some of the region's supplies.

In February, it has bought two cargoes totalling 150,000 barrels at $2.75 to $3.16 per barrel over Singapore naphtha quotes on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis to Batangas where Caltex runs its 70,000-bpd refinery.
Caltex is sourcing its supplies from its refineries in Thailand, South Korea and Singapore through its affiliate in Singapore.
A major in Singapore also sought a 25-30,000-tonne cargo for Australia for either February or March lifting.

A Caltex company source said Caltex Philippines has already stepped up its its gasoline imports for January and February due ot the turnaround of a 35,000-barrels-per-day crude unit and three secondary units January 20-30.
Caltex normally imports around 100,000 barrels per month of 95-octane unleaded gasoline, but for January it imported 100,000 barrels of reformate and 83,000 barrels of gasoline, the source said.
But refiners said supplies in Singapore and China were tight. Only a 20,000 tonne cargo of 90-octane gasoline from Shanghai was heard offered for lifting end February.
In comparison, naphtha was well supplied with little end-user demand seen.
Bangladesh emerged with a tender to sell 85,000 barrels of naphtha lifting February 16-18 from Chittagong which closes January 30.

A Singapore refiner with second-half February barrels offered last week at 70 cents per barrel over Singapore spot quotes, fob, said it was rolling over its cargo into March as bids were only coming from 30 cents.
Traders said the market was flattening, with the backwardation narrowing in to 20 cents to flat from 40 cents last week and 80 cents two weeks ago.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
